facts.statement: The genus Avalonianus was originally described by Harry Seeley in 1898.
The genus name was later renamed by Oskar Kuhn in 1961 because the original name was preoccupied.
Avalonianus is considered a dubious or invalid genus of archosaur from the Late Triassic Westbury Formation of England.
facts.quote: Avalonianus is a highly dubious and possibly invalid genus of archosaur from the Late Triassic Westbury Formation of England.

facts.statement: Subsequent analyses demonstrated that the remains were a paleontological chimera of Camelotia material and teeth from an archosaur or a possible primitive theropod.
facts.quote: Posteriores análisis demostraron que se trataba de una quimera paleontológica de restos del Camelotia y dientes de un arcosaurio o un posible terópodo primitivo.

facts.statement: The genus Avalonianus is classified within the parent group Saurischia.
The type species for the genus Avalonianus is Avalonia sanfordi.

rejected.statement: Later analysis revealed that the original description was a chimera, combining teeth from a non-dinosaurian ornithosuchian or early theropod with post-cranial remains of a prosauropod.
rejected.quote: It was thought to be a prosauropod, but later analysis revealed it was actually a chimera, with the original teeth coming from a non-dinosaurian ornithosuchian (or possibly an early theropod), and later-referred post-cranial prosauropod remains.
